cases.rationale: The request query determines the identifier in ORDER BY.
A request value occupies a bound LIKE parameter.
An untrusted value is substituted by str.format before execute.
Both possible table identifiers are locally fixed.
The request header flows into the SQL text through concatenation.
The request count is converted to an ordinary integer before interpolation.
A trusted parameter placeholder protects one filter but raw input supplies the order clause.
The branch selects complete literal queries; the week remains parameterized.
A request value is placed in a text node of a text/html response.
html.escape encodes the dynamic text node.
Markup takes an already formatted string containing request-derived text.
Markup.format escapes an ordinary (non-Markup) request value in a text node.
A raw cookie value is concatenated into Flask's default HTML response.
HTML-like characters are delivered with an explicit text/plain content type.
Only the title is escaped; the subtitle in the next text node is raw.
Flask's autoescaped template substitutes its argument into a text node.
An administrative digest is rebuilt before any caller identity is checked.
getServerSession followed by an early return for every non-editor guards the mutation.
A router that can archive a review accepts requests without any authentication middleware.
Passport JWT authentication on the exact mutation route is required before its handler.
A session is retrieved only to annotate logging; callers without a session still reach the mutation.
The authenticated server session supplies the account ID and absence of an ID terminates the request.
The administrative clear action trusts an account identifier in the request body without authenticating.
An established Passport session and req.user are required on every path to updateProfile.
Incoming billing events are committed directly from request JSON with no signature validation.
Stripe constructEvent verifies the raw text, signature and configured endpoint secret before dispatch.
The presence of an event ID supports tracing but supplies no authenticity proof.
Compares a SHA-256 HMAC of the original bytes with the supplied signature before enqueueing.
The signature header must be present but its contents are never validated.
The Octokit webhook verifier must accept the original payload before it can reach delivery handling.
A well-formed body is accepted as an authenticated build event.
Stripe authenticates the exact raw request bytes before the verified event is processed.
The fallible Stripe verification returns the only event added to the process-local ledger.
Reading a signature header and parsing JSON does not authenticate this direct HTTP route.
The awaited async construction must complete before the event is recorded.
The raw event is added to the local queue before the SDK can reject it.

An SDK exception falls back to the unverified payload and still updates the in-memory checkout count.
The callback accepts a payload only after the SDK resolves to true for its raw body.
The SDK resolves false on an invalid signature, but the route records the issue irrespective of that result.
The SDK dispatches to the registered handler only after verifying the incoming delivery.
Direct receive dispatches the unverified parsed body to the registered listener.
Only the true branch of the awaited verifier records a review; the false branch exits separately.
Payload processing continues when the allow-list header matches, with no authentication.
The verifier throws on invalid input and its authenticated result is the only update source.
The presence of the delivery ID is the only gate before recording label data.
The synchronous SDK must verify the unmodified text and incoming headers before it can be parsed for indexing.
The handler records a summary after both the success and exception paths.
Verification errors terminate the HTTP route before its local processing step.
The signed-payload branch is optional; an unsigned digest still updates the local record.
An Express webhook feeds an unverified payment event into the ledger.
The endpoint checks only the existence of a Stripe signature before using JSON.
The signed SDK event is constructed from raw body bytes and then consumed.
Asynchronous SDK verification completes before the event type is read.
An informational GET route serves static instructions without handling events.

A display helper formats an already stored GitHub delivery and has no inbound route.
A Svix delivery ID identifies unsigned JSON accepted into an in-memory map.
Checking signature header presence alone does not authenticate the submitted event.
The SDK verifies the raw body against its signed headers before processing.
An aliased Svix SDK constructor authenticates the same body and headers used by the endpoint.

Express processes incoming Stripe event types without authenticity verification.
Express processes Svix deliveries after checking only the message identifier.
Express serves a read-only status endpoint for registered webhook integrations.
